newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S RENEL LIKELY TO IMPORT 340,000T FUEL OIL.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S RENEL LIKELY TO IMPORT 340,000T FUEL OIL.

text.p: Cuts in gas supplies to Romania's Renel RA electricity authority might force the company to import an extra 340,000 tonnes fuel oil this winter in addition to a planned 1.3 million, an official said.

Renel president Victor Romert said power plants had already used part of strategic stocks of fuel oil as a substitute for natural gas following failure of the state-run Romgaz RA gas authority to maintain a constant flow of locally-produced gas.

"We will have to import some 340,000 tonnes of fuel oil in the coming months to make up for disruptions in gas supplies. It would mean a financial effort worth $50 million," Romert told a news conference.
Over the past 10 days Romgaz has halved its daily supplies of 20 million cubic metres to Renel on grounds that gas consumption has increased due to the cold weather, he said.

"The gas we get now comes mainly from imports. Romgas always has problems with local production during winter time," another Renel official told Reuters. "But I believe we will get through the winter withtout a crisis."
Romgaz officials were unavailable for comment.
Romert said coal supplies to Renel had also declined over the past few days.

"We receive some 20 percent less coal than planned every day," Romert said, adding that present stocks at plants stood at 6.0 million tonnes lignite and 680,000 tonnes of hard coal. Fuel oil stocks totalled 580,000 tonnes, he said.
On Tuesday, Renel signed a $160 million syndicated loan to import 1.3 million tonnes of fuel oil this winter.
The loan was arranged by ING Bank , along with Bank of America NT&SA, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi and BHF-Bank Aktiengesellschaft.

The loan will help Romania avoid a repeat of last winter's energy crisis when an acute hard currency shortage forced the country to reduce fuel imports drastically. Renel cut electricity supplies to most industries over January-March. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
